title: Shelled on the Winter Line: the 67th CA (AA)'s batteries by Venafro and Acquafondata, February 1944

participants.name: Battery A, 67th CA (AA)
participants.note: strafed and shelled on the road to Sant'Elia, 8 Feb

paras.text: Two batteries of the 2nd Battalion, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) (from 20 March 1944 the 894th AAA AW Bn), giving antiaircraft protection to the field artillery in the hills between Venafro and Cassino, and what the German XIV Panzer Corps reported about its fire on the same days. Battery E was at Lucenteforte, by Venafro, with half its guns detached near Sant'Elia from 10 to 23 Feb; it had men wounded on 14 and 16 Feb. Battery H moved up near Acquafondata on 12 Feb; its gun positions were shelled at 1500 on 21 Feb. Hand-edited; every entry cites its page in `ref`. Fields as in `records/README.md` ("An engagement"); `of` is each actor's nationality (`us`, `de`).

- `events.yml`: the batteries' moves and casualties, and the German reports of the same days, in the record's words. `placed` = `seq` when the record gives no time. - `positions.csv`: the batteries' stations as the forms name them (placed at the place name: the gun positions aren't given) and the German reports' places. The German reports give places as points of their reference-point map, the Bezugspunktkarte (`XXIII 117`); these are decoded with `tools/bezugspunkt.py` (`guides/BEZUGSPUNKTE.md`), `basis` `derived`. - `claims.yml`: the questions the records leave open (whether the fire on Vallerotonda was what hit Battery H; where Battery E's men were hit).

Context, not identification: no German report of these days names Venafro, Lucenteforte or Acquafondata, or an antiaircraft battery, so a German entry is "the same day and nearly the same place" at most. The batteries' stations are in `../../army/stations.csv` (units `67ca-e`, `67ca-h`), their casualties in `../../army/actions.csv`. The German frames: NARA T-314 roll 544 (XIV Panzer Corps' Taktische Meldungen, Feb 1944) and T-312 roll 90 (the Bezugspunktkarte).

events.words: "Lucenteforte, Italy. Left Venafro 1610 arr Lucenteforte 1610 Distance 3 miles. In tactical position giving AA protection to 1st Bn 178th FA."
events.source: Battery E, 67th CA (AA), morning report (record of events), 17 Jan 1944

events.words: "Vehicles and personnel strafed and shelled by enemy en route to St. Elia between 1300 and 1600 hrs on the road Aquafondata and St. Elia. Five EM hospitalized as a result of wounds received during the activity."
events.source: Battery A, 67th CA (AA), morning report (record of events), 8 Feb 1944

events.words: Moved 9 Feb from Acquafondata "to vicinity of St. Elia, Italy" (11 miles), in position 0300 10 Feb; rejoined the battery near Lucenteforte 0800 23 Feb.
events.source: Battery E morning report, record of events 24 Feb 1944

events.words: "Btry CP moved up with guns near Aquafondata. Left Pozzilli 0900 hrs, in position 1200 hrs." (The Second Platoon had gone up on 10 Feb, p0963.)
events.source: Battery H, 67th CA (AA), morning report (record of events), 12 Feb 1944

events.original: Starker Lkw.Verkehr in XXIII 97 ... 2 Feindbatterien bekämpft, 2 Lkw.in Brand geschossen.
events.translation: Heavy truck traffic in XXIII 97 [Sant'Elia] ... two enemy batteries engaged, two trucks set on fire.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Tagesmeldung vom 14.2.44

events.original: Mit einbrechender Dämmerung wurden im Raum XXIII 97 marschierende Feindkräfte in Stärke von 2 Batlnen. durch gutliegendes eigenes Artl.Feuer gefasst und zersprengt.
events.translation: At dusk enemy forces of two battalions marching in the area XXIII 97 [Sant'Elia] were caught by well-placed own artillery fire and scattered.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Nachmeldung zur Tagesmeldung vom 14.2.44

events.words: One man to hospital "Wounded in Action 1740", a sergeant "Wounded in Action (LW) and remaind on dy 1740". No cause typed.
Two men "Wounded in Action (LW) and remaind on dy". No time or cause typed.

events.original: Kan.Bttrn. bekämpften 2 Feindbattrn. im Raum XXIII 122, 1 im Raum XXIII 112 und 1 bei XXIII 117. Eigener Verschuss etwa 5000 Schuss.
events.translation: Our gun batteries engaged two enemy batteries in the area XXIII 122, one in XXIII 112 and one at XXIII 117. Own expenditure about 5,000 rounds.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: Arko 414 (corps artillery commander), Tagesmeldung vom 16.2.44

events.words: "Battery heavily shelled by enemy FA action between 1430 & 1500 hrs. Type of ammo used by enemy presumably 88's. Location of btry position believed to be revealed to the enemy as a result of (2) clip-winged Spitfires with proper British insignia"

events.original: Eigene Artl. ... vernichtet 1 Feindbatterie ... Lebhafter Lkw.Verkehr auf Nachschubstrasse nördl. XXIII 89
events.translation: Own artillery ... destroyed one enemy battery ... Busy truck traffic on the supply road north of XXIII 89 [Cassino].
events.note: Two passages of the one report, abridged with "..."; no square or time for the battery.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Tagesmeldung vom 17.2.44

events.original: Auf Strasse XXIII 89 nach XXIII 97, 15 mit Truppen beladenen LKw. beobachtet. Eigene Artl. bekämpfte von XXIII 97 nach XXIII 9 d marschierende Gruppen (15o bis 2oo Mann), zersprengte eine Tragtierkolonne von 4o Tieren u. 3o Mann, schoss 4 Lkw. in Brand und vernichtete eine Feindbatterie und 1 Einzelgeschütz. ... auffallend starke Verwendung von Phosphorbrand-Munition
events.translation: On the road from XXIII 89 [Cassino] to XXIII 97 [Sant'Elia], 15 lorries loaded with troops seen. Own artillery engaged groups of 150 to 200 men marching from XXIII 97 [Sant'Elia] toward XXIII 9? [the second digit unclear], scattered a pack-animal column of 40 animals and 30 men, set 4 lorries on fire and destroyed an enemy battery and one single gun. ... strikingly heavy use of phosphorus incendiary ammunition [by the enemy]
events.note: Two passages of the one report, abridged with "...". No square or time for the battery and the gun.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Tagesmeldung vom 18.2.44

events.words: "Battery and immediate vic heavily shelled by German FA from 0900 to 0930. Approximately 30 shells ... From 1400 to 1515, the battery again was subjected to heavy enemy FA action. Approx. 50 shells ... Action again believed to be result of direct ground observation." A 90 mm gun hit directly; one man killed, two hospitalized, six wounded who stayed on duty (p0630).

events.original: Während der Mittagstunden starker Verkehr auf Strasse XXIII 117 nach XXIII 97 ... Eigene Artl. legt Störungsfeuer auf XXIII 117 und Nachschubstrassen und zerstört 6 Lkw.
events.translation: At midday heavy traffic on the road from XXIII 117 [Vallerotonda] to XXIII 97 [Sant'Elia] ... Own artillery lays harassing fire on XXIII 117 and the supply roads and destroys 6 trucks.
events.note: The date is typed over: 21 or 22 Feb.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: 5. Geb.Div., Tagesmeldung vom 2?.2.44

events.original: 14.oo Uhr 4 erkannte Feindbatterien wurden von eigener Artl. bekämpft.
events.translation: At 14.00 four identified enemy batteries were engaged by own artillery.
events.note: In the Cassino sector; no squares.
events.source: XIV Panzer Corps, tactical reports: Zwischenmeldung vom 21.2.44

events.words: "Gun Positions shelled by enemy art'y at 1500 hrs. Two casualties evacuated." On the form: "SW in head and left arm by enemy shell fire 1500 hrs"; "SW in abdomen by enemy shell fire 1500 hrs".
events.source: Battery H morning report, 21 Feb 1944 (form and record of events)

events.words: "Battery releived from mission of giving AA protection 178th FA 1st Bn."; to the Pozzilli-Casale road 26-27 Feb.
events.source: Battery E morning report, record of events 26 Feb 1944

claims.question: Was the German fire of 21 Feb on Vallerotonda what hit Battery H?
claims.answer: Battery H's gun positions near Acquafondata were shelled at 1500 on 21 Feb; two men seriously wounded
claims.note: The American side: time, place (near the village), and that it was artillery.

claims.question: Was the German fire of 21 Feb on Vallerotonda what hit Battery H?
claims.answer: The 5th Mountain Division laid harassing fire on XXIII 117 and the supply roads
claims.note: No time; the date is typed over (21 or 22 Feb). Harassing fire on a point and roads, not on a battery.

claims.question: Was the German fire of 21 Feb on Vallerotonda what hit Battery H?
claims.answer: XXIII 117 is Vallerotonda, about 3 km west of Acquafondata village
claims.note: Printed point 106 is the circle on Vallerotonda (XXIII = 8Z, less 11). Neither the battery's guns nor the German shells' fall are given closer than that.

claims.question: Was the German fire of 21 Feb on Vallerotonda what hit Battery H?
claims.answer: Other German artillery fired on American batteries that day: the 90th Panzergrenadier Division engaged four at 14.00
claims.note: In the Cassino sector, south-west of Acquafondata; no squares. Whether the two sides kept the same clock is not known, so the hour between 14.00 and 1500 settles nothing.

claims.question: Where were Battery E's men hit on 14 and 16 Feb: at Lucenteforte, or with the sections near Sant'Elia?
claims.answer: Sections 2, 4, 6 and 8 were in position in the vicinity of St. Elia from 0300 10 Feb to 0800 23 Feb
claims.source: Battery E morning report, record of events 24 Feb 1944
claims.note: Half the battery's guns, about 8 km from the rest at Lucenteforte.

claims.question: Where were Battery E's men hit on 14 and 16 Feb: at Lucenteforte, or with the sections near Sant'Elia?
claims.answer: The wound entries give no cause and no place
claims.source: Battery E morning reports, 14 and 16 Feb 1944
claims.note: Only "Wounded in Action" and, on 14 Feb, 1740.

claims.question: Where were Battery E's men hit on 14 and 16 Feb: at Lucenteforte, or with the sections near Sant'Elia?
claims.answer: At dusk on 14 Feb German artillery fired on troops marching at Sant'Elia (XXIII 97)
claims.note: Dusk and 1740 may be the same hour; if so, the sections near Sant'Elia were nearer that fire than the battery at Lucenteforte (about 18 km away). Inference: the reports don't say which men were where.

claims.question: Was the gun hit at St. Elia on 18 Feb the German report's 'Einzelgeschütz'?
claims.answer: Battery A (1st Bn) at St. Elia was shelled 0900-0930 and 1400-1515 on 18 Feb; a 90 mm gun "received direct hit causing piece to be temp. inactive"; one killed
claims.note: Shelling "believed to be result of direct ground observation" (the battery's belief).

claims.question: Was the gun hit at St. Elia on 18 Feb the German report's 'Einzelgeschütz'?
claims.answer: The 5th Mountain Division's artillery fired that day on troops marching out of XXIII 97 (Sant'Elia) and "vernichtete eine Feindbatterie und 1 Einzelgeschütz"
claims.note: No square or hour for the battery or the gun; the corps artillery commander's reports for 17-18 Feb, which on 16 Feb gave the squares, are not on the film (folios run 141/17 to 169/17 without them).

claims.question: Was the gun hit at St. Elia on 18 Feb the German report's 'Einzelgeschütz'?
claims.answer: Same day and area at most: the gun was "temp. inactive", not destroyed, and the German claim names no place
claims.note: A lead, not an identification: other Allied guns stood around Sant'Elia that day, and a destroyed-gun claim is the firer's claim.

positions.label: Venafro
positions.note: The town. Battery E's station to 16 Jan 1944.

positions.label: Battery E, 67th CA (AA), Lucenteforte
positions.source: Battery E morning reports; the place as printed on sheet 161-III
positions.note: The battery's station, 17 Jan - 26 Feb 1944, placed at the place name on the map (army/places.csv); the gun positions are not given.

positions.label: Battery E, sections 2, 4, 6 and 8, "vicinity of St. Elia"
positions.source: Battery E morning report, record of events 24 Feb 1944
positions.note: Half the battery's guns, 10-23 Feb, "in position" in the vicinity of St. Elia; placed at the town (the circle on the town on the Feb 1944 Bezugspunktkarte, t312-0090/f0215). Before that at Casale (from 15 Jan) and Acquafondata (from 24 Jan).

positions.label: Battery H, 67th CA (AA), "near Aquafondata"
positions.note: "Btry CP moved up with guns near Aquafondata": placed at the village (army/places.csv); the gun positions are not given. 12 Feb - 10 Mar 1944.

positions.label: XXIII 97 (Sant'Elia)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, Feb 1944 edition, 8Z 86 (XXIII 97 less 11), decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py
positions.note: Printed point 86, the circle on S. Elia Fiumerapido. Named in the 5th Mountain Division's reports of 14 and 21 Feb (t314-0544/f0361, f0362, f0486).

positions.label: XXIII 112 (east of Cassino)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, Feb 1944 edition, 8Z 101, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py
positions.note: One enemy battery engaged here on 16 Feb (t314-0544/f0406); a 17 cm battery fired on a battery here by sound-ranging in the night 15-16 Feb (f0392).

positions.label: XXIII 117 (Vallerotonda)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, Feb 1944 edition, 8Z 106, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py
positions.note: Printed point 106, the circle on Vallerotonda. One enemy battery engaged "bei XXIII 117" on 16 Feb (t314-0544/f0406); harassing fire on XXIII 117 and the supply roads on 21 or 22 Feb (f0486).

positions.label: XXIII 122 (south of Cervaro)
positions.source: Bezugspunktkarte, Feb 1944 edition, 8Z 111, decoded with tools/bezugspunkt.py
positions.note: Two enemy batteries engaged here on 16 Feb (t314-0544/f0406). The point's reading on the map is uncertain (the number sits below-right of its circle).

positions.label: Battery A, 67th CA (AA) (1st Bn), St. Elia
positions.note: A 90 mm battery of the regiment's 1st Battalion, at St. Elia 8-18 Feb 1944, placed at the town (army/places.csv); the gun position is not given. Context: not the 2nd Battalion.
